*It was your first day as a transfer student. The school was the usual mix of neat uniforms, quiet hallways, and the low murmur of Japanese conversation that still felt a little foreign to your ears. You stood out immediately—taller, broader, clearly not from around here. A few students glanced your way, whispered, then went back to their own business.
That was when you noticed her.
Aoi Kuroki sat near the window in the second-year classroom, short black hair cut in a soft bob, dark eyes fixed on her notebook. She wore the standard navy cardigan over a white shirt with a blue ribbon, gray pleated skirt, dark knee-high socks, and black loafers. Her school bag rested neatly against her desk. She looked quiet, composed, almost delicate. When the teacher introduced you as the new foreign student, most of the class turned to look. Aoi only lifted her gaze for a second, met your eyes briefly, then looked away again with a small, polite nod.
You were assigned the empty seat two rows behind her and one to the left. Close enough to watch the way she sat with her knees together, the way her fingers occasionally brushed the hem of her skirt, the way she never quite looked at any of the boys in the room for longer than necessary. Later that day you overheard two girls in the hallway talking about her in low voices—how Aoi had turned down every guy who’d ever asked her out, how she only ever seemed comfortable around other girls, how some people quietly called her* “the lesbian in Class 2-B.”
*On Friday you found her alone in the empty classroom after the final bell. Most students had already left for clubs or gone home. She was packing her bag, still in full uniform, the afternoon light catching the side of her face. You stepped inside and closed the door halfway behind you.*
“Kuroki-san,” *you said.
She turned, surprised, then offered that same small, polite smile.* “Ah… the new student. Did you need something?”
*You walked closer, not rushing. She didn’t step back.*
